Grouping, cgroup, branch stack, and address filter mechanics beyond accounting and detach calls.

findings.text: Local counter read routine is visible beyond its defining file for in-kernel callers needing atomic inspection without inheritance.

Local counter inspection is available only on the owning processor with scheduling activity frozen, and it succeeds only for non-inherited work owned by the caller with residency assurances for pinned work, returning the current count plus optional timing summaries, and otherwise signaling distinct unsupported, invalid, or busy failures.

Counter refresh distinguishes active residency from inactive parking, using cross-processor assistance for resident work and locked time reconciliation for parked work, with revalidation when state shifts during acquisition, ensuring observed counts reflect recent scheduling.
Processor-wide permission check is visible beyond its defining file for gating creation of processor-bound monitoring.
Processor-wide monitoring requires elevated privilege when system paranoia is restrictive, plus approval from the mandatory security hook for processor access, otherwise access is denied.

Task resolution treats an absent identifier as the current thread and otherwise looks up the named thread under read-side protection, holding a reference on success and reporting absence when no such thread exists.

Context acquisition separates processor-wide from thread-bound monitoring, requiring privilege validation for the former with pinned shared context, and for the latter reusing or installing a per-thread context with safe retry on races and rejection when the thread is exiting.

A freshly allocated monitoring context starts with initialized synchronization, empty membership for performance domains and event groupings, and a single owning reference, optionally bound to a referenced target thread.

Per-domain subcontexts bind a performance unit with empty linkage and activity sets plus a single reference, with processor-wide instances reusing embedded storage that never fails and thread-bound instances inserted in type order with reference sharing on match.

Domain subcontext lifetime is guarded by the parent context lock with interrupt protection during lookup, insertion, and release, using atomic reference counts where final release detaches linkage under lock and defers reclamation.
Reclamation of domain subcontexts is deferred to a grace period, distinguishing embedded processor storage from separately allocated thread storage for appropriate release.

Event teardown after a grace period releases namespace, address filtering ranges, and tracing filters where configured, before returning the event object to its cache, with filtering support varying by build configuration.

Sideband classification excludes inherited and thread-bound events and includes processor-wide events requesting execution, mapping, communication, or tracing observations, with detachment removing the event from per-processor sideband membership under lock.
Sideband membership changes are serialized by a per-processor list lock held across removal.

Frequency-driven event accounting maintains a global population count, clearing tick dependency only when the last such event departs on tickless-capable builds, with an extra spinlock guarding that transition.
Transition of the frequency event population to empty under tickless operation is serialized by a dedicated spinlock.

Auxiliary per-thread performance storage pairs a wrapper with cache-allocated payload, recording global scope and owning cache plus a single reference, with release freeing payload then wrapper and deferred release via grace period.

Installation of auxiliary thread storage uses atomic compare exchange with retry, sharing existing live storage and marking global scope when requested, replacing dead storage, and cleaning up promptly if the thread exits during installation.

Global auxiliary storage is reference counted with fast-path sharing and write-guarded installation across all threads, upgrading existing thread storage to global scope where present and rolling back on allocation failure, with removal clearing scope and detaching when the last user departs.

Global auxiliary storage traversal uses read-side protection while installation and removal hold a write guard for exclusive population changes, with per-thread detachment relying on atomic reference transitions.

Auxiliary storage attachment follows the event target, using thread-local installation for thread-bound targets and global installation otherwise with explicit global linkage marking, and detachment clears task linkage always and global linkage only when previously marked.

Event unaccounting skips inherited children and otherwise decrements global populations for mapping, communication, and tracing interests while treating scheduling, sideband, grouping, and stack interests as keeping the scheduler hook alive until the last such event departs with delayed deactivation.

Scheduler hook lifetime follows a shared count where arrival enables observation and departure either decrements directly or schedules delayed disabling when contention prevents immediate transition, with the delayed worker disabling only on reaching emptiness under mutex.

Exclusive performance units forbid mixing thread-bound and processor-wide monitoring through a signed population where one direction indicates thread ownership and the opposite indicates processor ownership, with acquisition failing when opposition exists and release restoring toward neutrality.

Final event release follows a strict order covering security notification, buffer and exclusive ownership cleanup, grouping and auxiliary storage detachment, custom destruction, target thread release, domain and parent context release, module release with list removal and wakeup, and deferred object reclamation.
Final release synchronizes pending asynchronous work, serializes ring buffer detachment with mapping mutex, and guards performance unit list removal with its spinlock plus wakeup for waiters.
Release expects a single remaining reference and intentionally leaks rather than freeing when the transition fails, avoiding use after free on unexpected sharing.
Module reference release is visible beyond its defining file for owners dropping dependencies on loadable performance units.
Module reference release tolerates absent owners and otherwise decrements only when positive, warning on underflow and emitting a trace with caller identity.

Inconsistent teardown such as mismatched parent linkage, lingering active membership, missing context linkage, or unexpected sharing triggers warnings while preserving safety by leaking or asserting rather than corrupting.

Counter inspection and context handling freeze scheduling with interrupt suppression for local reads, use interrupt-saving context locks for parked time updates and pinning, and use the thread mutex for installing new thread contexts.
Attach state encodes distinct task association, scheduling callback need, exclusive ownership, callchain need, task data linkage, and global data linkage interests.
Event lifetime distinguishes active residency on a processor from inactive parking off processor for read and timekeeping purposes.
Event attributes signal sideband and accounting interests for mapping, communication, grouping, switching, tracing, filtering, and stack capture behaviors.
